Chooses how the mip levels of a texture are read. With 0 the level that is closest to the size on the screen is used, with 1 two levels are blended (trilinear filtering), which hides the jump from one level to the next. It only has an effect on a texture that has mip levels: use flag 8 or a DDS file that stores them, see [Differences](Differences). This is a BlitzLLVM extension: the originals read every texture with the settings of its flags and do not have samplers.
| Mode | Result |
|---|---|
| 0 | Nearest: the texel that is closest, which shows blocks. |
| 1 | Linear: blends the texels around the point, the default. |

@param sampler  The sampler to change.
@param mode     The filter mode from the table above.
@gap The mode has to be 0 or 1, other values stop the program with an error.
